evals.prompt: Create a new SPEC.yaml for a skill called 'rate-limiter' that should limit API calls to 100 per minute per user, return 429 on overflow, and persist counters in Redis.
evals.expected_output: Generates a SPEC.yaml with specification block (name, version), requirements with IDs (RATE-001, RATE-002, RATE-003), Given/When/Then scenarios for each requirement covering the happy path, overflow case, and Redis persistence.

assertions.criteria: Requirements include scenarios with given/when/then format, covering the 100/min limit, 429 response, and Redis persistence cases.
Each requirement has a unique ID like RATE-001 following the kebab-case convention.

evals.prompt: I have an existing auth service that uses password login. I need to add OAuth support and remove the legacy token system. Create a delta spec for this change.
evals.expected_output: Creates a delta_specs section with added (OAuth support), modified (password login now also accepts OAuth), and removed (legacy token system) entries, all referencing existing requirement IDs.

assertions.criteria: The delta spec's 'added' section contains OAuth authentication requirement.
The delta spec's 'removed' section references the legacy token requirement with a reason.

evals.prompt: Fix a typo in the variable name 'counnter' → 'counter' in my Python script.
evals.expected_output: Simple text substitution, no TDD/SDD workflow needed. Skill should NOT trigger.

assertions.text: Does not invoke TDD/SDD workflow for trivial fix
assertions.criteria: The response performs the rename directly without creating SPEC.yaml, test stubs, or invoking TDD cycle.
